citation: Anirban Chatterjee (Sonar), 'State of Code Developer Survey report: The current reality of AI coding', Sonar blog, 8 January 2026. https://www.sonarsource.com/blog/state-of-code-developer-survey-report-the-current-reality-of-ai-coding/ (companion press release: https://www.sonarsource.com/company/press-releases/sonar-data-reveals-critical-verification-gap-in-ai-coding/)
source_tier: Company research (vendor survey summary blog; full PDF report not opened)
access_status: Fully read the blog summary page. The full downloadable report and the press release were not opened directly; [uncertain] whether the full report has methodology detail the blog lacks.
sponsor_and_incentive: Run and published by Sonar (SonarSource), which sells code quality and verification tooling (SonarQube). The finding that verification is a bottleneck supports its product. The blog also claims SonarQube users are 44% less likely to have outages caused by AI code, a self-serving comparison with no method given.
exact_quotes: "96% of developers do not fully trust AI-generated code, and only 48% always verify it before committing." (Key findings, blog, as relayed). "38% of developers report that reviewing AI code requires more effort than reviewing code written by human colleagues." (verification section). "Rather than delivering a direct productivity boost, the surge in AI-generated code has created a verification bottleneck." (TL;DR). Sample: "more than 1,100 professional developers." [uncertain: quotes taken from a fetch tool that summarises pages, so wording and location should be re-checked against the live page before publication]
date_and_recency: Published 8 January 2026. Fieldwork dates not stated on the blog page. [uncertain]
key_claims: Developers use AI heavily but do not trust it. Verification, not generation, is now the bottleneck. 72% of those who have tried AI tools use them daily; developers say 42% of committed code is AI-generated or AI-assisted and expect 65% by 2027. Trust and effectiveness vary by task. A vendor claim that SonarQube users report better outcomes.
headline_figures: 96% do not fully trust AI-generated code (self-reported; trust in functional correctness per press release). 48% always verify before committing. 38% say reviewing AI code takes more effort than reviewing human colleagues' code. 42% of committed code AI-generated or assisted (developer estimate). 65% expected by 2027 (developer prediction). 72% of AI tool triers use daily. Use by project type: 88% prototypes, 83% internal non-critical, 73% customer-facing, 58% business-critical. 90% use AI for new code but 55% of them rate it extremely or very effective; 72% use for refactoring, 43% rate highly effective; documentation 74%, explaining code 66%, tests 59%. 35% use personal accounts rather than sanctioned tools (from press coverage, not in the blog text read). 64% use agentic tools (chapter title only). 44% fewer AI-caused outages for SonarQube users (vendor claim).
sample_unit_and_population: More than 1,100 professional developers. Countries, sampling method, seniority mix, question wording and response rate not stated on the blog page. [uncertain]
observed_vs_stated: Entirely stated (self-reported survey). No observed behaviour. The 42% share and 2027 forecast are developer estimates.
what_makes_trust_justified: The source's implied answer is systematic verification before commit, supported by automated code quality and review tooling. It reports use is lower for business-critical work (58%), suggesting developers ration trust by stakes.
what_it_costs: Review effort: 38% say AI code takes more effort to review than colleagues' code. The blog frames this as a verification bottleneck that offsets generation gains. No hours or delay measured.
failure_mode_class: Over-reliance and unverified wrong code (functional correctness); shadow AI use via personal accounts as a governance risk.
control_that_would_have_prevented: Not an incident study. Not applicable. The implied control is checking every AI change before commit, plus sanctioned accounts.
limitations_stated: The blog page states no methodology beyond sample size. Developer forecasts (65% by 2027) are predictions. No limitations section found on the page. [uncertain: full report may differ]
counter_evidence: The Register (9 Jan 2026) noted the figures come from a vendor selling verification software. Self-report cannot show whether the 48% who say they always check actually do. The 44% outage reduction for SonarQube users has no stated controls. No independent replication read.
verification_status: Core figures (96%, 48%, 38%, 42%, sample size, date) checked against the Sonar blog page opened this session via a summarising fetch tool, and they match the press release headline in search results. 35% personal accounts and 65% by 2027 come from search summary or TL;DR only. [uncertain] The full report PDF and The Register article were not opened.
usable_claim: In a January 2026 Sonar survey of more than 1,100 developers, 96% said they do not fully trust AI-generated code and 48% said they always verify it before committing; 38% said reviewing AI code takes more effort than reviewing a colleague's. These are self-reported figures from a vendor that sells verification tools.
do_not_use: The 44% fewer outages for SonarQube users (vendor claim, no method). The 65% by 2027 as fact (forecast). The 35% personal accounts figure until checked in the full report. Any reading that 48% shows developers skip checking: it is a stated habit.
overlap_with_existing_essays: [uncertain] Per the task note, this overlaps the Verification Gap essay, which already uses 96%, 48% and 38%. New material not used there is likely: usage by project criticality, effectiveness by task, the 58% business-critical figure. Not checked against the essay text or Checking Isn't Catching.
